text:
maria: Heads-up — legal asked if we can set per-API-key overrides for a handful of internal partners (service accounts), specifically higher burst windows but the same long-term qps. They want the partner keys to not get throttled during short heavy backfills. Thoughts on policy + enforcement?

todd: we already have per-org quotas, right? per-key would be a new layer. are these partner keys tied to orgs or mapped to a special service-account org?

maria: tied to internal orgs but different teams. Legal is pushing for explicit key-level controls so they can grant exceptions without changing org-wide limits.

cheng: sounds reasonable. main questions: precedence (key override vs org config), storage (config service vs k/v in the gateway), and how bursts are tracked (sliding window counters vs token bucket).

sarah: operationally we prefer token-bucket for burst allowances. easier to reason about and compatible with autoscaling heuristics. we prob want two numbers: steady_qps and burst_capacity (tokens).

leo: +1 token-bucket. also need audit logs when overrides are granted. we should surface override metadata in the Console (who granted, TTL, reason).

maria: Agreed. UX ask: product wants a "key overrides" view in the Console and an API to programmatically set overrides for partners. Also want an ability to set temporary overrides that expire automatically.

todd: implementation idea: extend current quota config JSON with per_key_overrides map. sample:
```yaml
rate_limit:
  default_qps: 50
  burst_tokens: 100
  per_key_overrides:
    key: "svc-partner-123"
      override_qps: 200
      burst_tokens: 1000
      expires_at: "2026-01-15T00:00:00Z"
```
Note: would need to validate tokens won't exceed a global safety cap.

cheng: minor correction to YAML indentation but yes. enforcement in the edge gateway should check: 1) key-level override if exists and not expired 2) org-level limits 3) fallback default. Precedence: key -> org -> default.

leo: what about billing? if a partner uses more tokens during bursts, do we charge them the same? Legal wants cost predictability. maybe we allow burst but cap billable tokens per day?

sarah: we can expose "burst_non_billable" flag per override, but ops has to accept potential cost. I'd rather keep billing separate and surface estimates in Console.

quota-bot: [alert] enforcement spike detected for svc-partner-123: 900rps sustained for 45s, enforced by key-override token bucket.

maria: that alert proves this will happen. we need telemetry: per-key SLOs, daily usage, max burst events, and a mitigation alert when override-exhausted -> automatic fallback.

todd: follow-ups for sprint: (1) schema change to config service (2) gateway check order + fast path for overrides (3) Console UI + audit trail (4) tests for TTL expiry and safety cap. who owns?

cheng: I'll pick up gateway + tests. todd can handle schema + migration. sara(h) can shepherd the Console UX with product. leo do you own the audit/logging?

leo: yes, I'll add the audit events and a new dashboard tile: "Key override usage" with columns [key, owner, override_qps, burst_tokens, expires_at, current_tokens, 24h_billable_tokens].

maria: perfect. one more ask from legal: ability to set an "emergency canary" key for partners that bypasses org fallback (for incident response). this should be opt-in and logged.

cheng: that's just another flag on the override: emergency_bypass: true. however we'll require 2FA approval flow and a TTL of <= 1h. put that in the API contract.

leo: note: if we allow bypass we must rate-limit the bypass itself (e.g., hard cap 5k rps) to avoid runaway.

maria: ok team — can we put a short RFC doc in #eng-platform-design and link it here by EOD? I'll loop legal and product after that.

todd: yup, drafting now. putting a design PR and will ping. :thumbsup:

quota-bot: [info] draft RFC created: https://go/repo/patch/12345 (maria, todd)

maria: thanks. closing thread for now, will reopen with RFC comments. :wave:
